name: Shivani Sehgal
remarks: A blocker is any condition that caps the maximum disposition this run may lawfully report, regardless of how much work is done or how good the result looks, because the contract treats the missing thing as unproven rather than merely untidy. It is not the same as a finding, which is one individual defect the gate prints, nor the same as a named coverage gap, which is my own declaration in EDICT.md that some obligation went unmet. A blocker is the causal link between those and the ceiling: the parent gate mints a ceiling token, the report must copy that token verbatim, and so long as any error-severity finding stands the token is BLOCK and no phase work is lawful. Blockers come in three shapes here. First, authority blockers, where the artifact that would clear the finding belongs to another instrument, so writing it would itself be a contract violation, which covers 24 of the 29. Second, signature blockers, where the remedy exists and is well defined but requires a cryptographic act by an enrolled principal whose key is absent, which covers the remaining 5 and which no amount of code can substitute for, because the entire point of a signature is that it cannot be manufactured by the party being checked. Third, evidence blockers, which are structural rather than mechanical: the batch scopes 10 slots against a mandated minimum of 20, every slot carries the archetype cross-repository-repair which is outside the closed AR1 to AR10 set and therefore takes 10 of 10 slots against a one-fifth ceiling, and invariant 8 holds that SHIP requires an external signed pilot over frozen bytes, so no local pass, self-solve, or authored probability can ever produce it. The practical consequence is that clearing all 29 findings would move this run from BLOCK to at best HOLD:PILOT_REQUIRED, never to SHIP, and the batch would still have to be re-scoped and re-archetyped before it could close as a conforming batch.

- Nothing is dropped silently anymore. Every skipped file now gets a presence marker: ----- DELIVERABLE: <file> (<size> bytes, present — contents not included: <reason>) -----. Reasons include size cap, unreadable, not extractable, evidence budget, and image limit.

- Root scan cap: _ROOT_SCAN_MAX_FILE_BYTES changed from 512,000 to 100,000 bytes. It now applies only to text files in the root scan.
- Documents: PDF, DOCX, XLSX and PPTX files are no longer skipped for their size on disk. _EXTRACT_CHAR_CAP changed from 100,000 to 150,000 characters, and the header now says when extracted text was cut.
